# `silk/i64`

<!-- Generated by packages/compiler/scripts/generate-documentation.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Sixty-four-bit signed integers for large fixed-width values and exact integer protocols.

## When to use

Use `i64` when a stable signed 64-bit range is part of storage, interchange, or arithmetic.
Prefer `isize` only for target-sized offsets; its width changes with the compilation target.

## Details

Ordinary arithmetic, narrowing conversions, division by zero, and invalid shift counts trap.
`checked*` returns [`Option`](./option.md#declaration-73696c6b2f6f7074696f6e3a3a4f7074696f6e) instead, `wrapping*` uses arithmetic modulo 2^64, and `saturating*`
clamps at [`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6936343a3a4d494e) or [`MAX`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6936343a3a4d4158). Signed right shifts preserve the sign bit.

Decimal [`parse`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6936343a3a7061727365) consumes the whole input and reports syntax separately from range overflow.
[`toText`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6936343a3a746f54657874) allocates owned text. Conversion to `f32` or `f64` can round large exact integers.

## Gotchas

[`MIN`](#declaration-73696c6b2f6936343a3a4d494e) has no positive i64 counterpart. Its ordinary negation and division by `-1` trap.

Import as `i64` with `import silk.i64`.

Public declarations: 60.

<a id="declaration-73696c6b2f6936343a3a4d4158"></a>

## `MAX`

```silk
pub const MAX: i64
```

The largest i64. The checked arithmetic intrinsics reject every result above this bound.
